observations.content: User supplied preparation turns 1–9/12 as context-only reference for a later explicit implementation task on the observational-memory repository; no implementation prompt has yet been given, and the assistant acknowledged each packet with CONTEXT_RECEIVED.

Historical task requirements: expose actual pi usage cost from every observer/consolidator worker run to the parent, including ephemeral and unsuccessful runs when valid usage exists; persist valid costs in session-ledger entries with role/run identity; aggregate costs across all branches including abandoned branches; ignore missing, malformed, non-finite, or negative values; surface total in status/footer UI; add focused tests for aggregation, invalid entries, handoff, and display.

PLAN.md describes observational-memory architecture: phased short-term observer→ledger→injection→compaction then long-term consolidator→.memory topic files; bespoke child_process.spawn of ordinary recorded pi sessions; vendored trimmed OM ledger modules; shared worker extension selected by OM_WORKER and separate orchestrator; orchestrator assigns unique timestamp IDs; strong Claude Sonnet 4.6 default models; per-session default-OFF /om gate; Phase B uses INDEX.md and descriptive JOURNEY.md, neither rolled back by /tree.

Repository excerpts describe core implementation: src/index.ts orchestrates commands/hooks and persisted om.enabled gate; observer-trigger dispatches bounded parallel chunks and commits observations; consolidator-trigger promotes oldest overflow and tombstones handed still-active observations on clean exit; compaction-hook snaps cutoff to chunk boundaries and has observer-wait fast path; compaction-trigger may resume mid-run compaction; ledger fold/projection/pool/progress/render support branch-local observations, tombstones, clocks, compaction and timeline.

Worker subprocesses are launched headlessly via pi -e agent/index.ts -p with builtins/extensions/skills/templates/context files disabled; sessions remain in the global store. Observer results use atomic IPC files in .memory/.runs; consolidator has scoped .memory-only read/write/edit/ls/grep tools and writes topic files plus JOURNEY.md. Memory paths use atomic writes; INDEX.md is orchestrator-owned and JOURNEY.md is excluded from topic listing.

The supplied project excerpts include README documentation and broad Vitest coverage for timestamp IDs, folding/projection/progress, cutoff waiting, scoped consolidator tools, memory paths/rendering, pool selection, worker launch/result IPC, footer gauges, and timeline. Config defaults and excerpts are reference data; some README/PLAN values differ from src/config.ts defaults, so retain source as supplied rather than assuming they are consistent.
